title: Parameterized Shortest Path Heuristics in Sparse Directed Graphs: Theoretical Foundations and Empirical Evaluation
content_text: We study shortest-path computation on sparse directed graphs with bounded treewidth within the context of CS301 (cs.DM). Existing approaches frequently suffer from degraded tail performance, high memory amplification, or brittle worst-case guarantees when deployed on realistic workloads. In this paper (arXiv:2502.00001v2), we propose a principled framework based on O(m + n log n) priority-queue relaxations and bidirectional frontier pruning. First, we formalize the invariant conditions required for correctness and derive tight analytical bounds on time and space complexity. Second, we present an implementation tailored for modern multi-core and hierarchical storage environments, demonstrating how careful data-structure layout eliminates redundant synchronization and I/O bottlenecks. Experimental evaluation across synthetic and production-derived benchmarks shows consistent improvements in throughput, 99th-percentile latency, and resource utilization compared to classical baselines.
tldr_summary: Introduces O(m + n log n) priority-queue relaxations and bidirectional frontier pruning for shortest-path computation on sparse directed graphs with bounded treewidth (cs.DM), proving tight complexity bounds and improving tail latency and throughput on CS301 benchmarks.
source_authors: Priya Iyer, Siddharth Deshmukh, Pooja Menon

Experimental evaluation across synthetic and production-derived benchmarks shows consistent improvements in throughput, 99th-percentile latency, and resource utilization compared to classical baselines.
tldr_summary: Introduces aborting defective releases within 90 seconds of synthetic traffic anomalies for sequential probability ratio testing on http latency and error-rate metrics (cs.SE), proving tight complexity bounds and improving tail latency and throughput on SE101 benchmarks.
source_authors: Aarav Lindqvist, Divya Verma
